_meta.description: RetroDojo emulated systems reference dataset. Tracks every platform that can be emulated on retro handhelds — organized by platform type (console, handheld, PC), generation era, and emulation maturity. Used to cross-reference emulators.json and chipsets.json.

platform_types.console: Home consoles connected to a TV/monitor.
platform_types.handheld: Portable gaming devices with built-in screens.
platform_types.pc: Personal computer platforms and compatibility layers.

emulation_maturity.mature: Emulation is highly accurate, well-optimized, and stable. Most games work perfectly.
emulation_maturity.good: Emulation works well for most titles with minor issues. Active development continues.
emulation_maturity.developing: Emulation is functional but has significant gaps. Rapid improvement expected.
emulation_maturity.experimental: Early-stage emulation. Many games are broken or unplayable. Use at own risk.
emulation_maturity.reimplementation: Not traditional emulation — engine reimplementation or compatibility layer.

systems.name: Nintendo Entertainment System
systems.emulation_notes: Cycle-accurate emulation achieved years ago. Virtually all licensed and homebrew titles work. Mapper support is comprehensive.

systems.name: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
systems.emulation_notes: Enhancement chip games (Super FX, SA-1, DSP) all supported. bsnes offers cycle-accurate emulation. Snes9x is lighter and better for low-end devices.
known_limitations: bsnes cycle-accurate mode can be heavier than expected on very low-end SoCs

systems.name: Sega Genesis
systems.emulation_notes: Near-perfect emulation. Sega CD and 32X add-ons also well-supported via PicoDrive/Genesis Plus GX.

systems.name: Sega Master System
systems.emulation_notes: Fully mature. Genesis Plus GX handles SMS as a subset of its Genesis emulation.

systems.name: Neo Geo
systems.emulation_notes: Both AES (home) and MVS (arcade) variants emulated perfectly. Neo Geo CD also supported.

systems.name: Atari 2600
systems.emulation_notes: Trivial to emulate on any hardware. Stella is cycle-accurate.

systems.name: Atari 7800
systems.emulation_notes: Backwards compatible with 2600. Emulation is complete and mature.

systems.name: PlayStation
systems.emulation_notes: DuckStation is the gold standard — supports PGXP geometry correction, upscaling, texture replacement. Nearly every game works perfectly.
known_limitations: A few games with obscure protection schemes may need specific BIOS versions

systems.name: Nintendo 64
systems.gpu: Reality Co-Processor (RCP) — Reality Signal Processor + Reality Display Processor
systems.emulation_notes: The RDP (Reality Display Processor) makes accurate emulation surprisingly demanding. ParaLLEl uses Vulkan compute for RDP accuracy. Mupen64Plus is lighter but less accurate.
known_limitations: Some games require specific RSP/RDP plugin combinations
Expansion Pak games (Majora's Mask, Perfect Dark) are more demanding
Cycle-accurate RDP emulation via ParaLLEl needs Vulkan compute support

systems.name: Sega Saturn
systems.emulation_notes: Dual-CPU architecture made emulation historically difficult. Beetle Saturn (Mednafen) is accurate but heavy. YabaSanshiro is lighter for handhelds but less accurate.
known_limitations: Dual-SH2 synchronization causes compatibility issues in some games
Heavy for low-end ARM SoCs compared to PS1
Some 3D-heavy games require per-game settings

systems.name: Sega Dreamcast
systems.emulation_notes: Flycast is excellent and well-optimized. Most games run at full speed on mid-range ARM SoCs. NAOMI arcade board also supported.
known_limitations: Some VMU-dependent features may not work perfectly
Light gun games need touch/pointer mapping

systems.name: Nintendo GameCube
systems.emulation_notes: Dolphin is one of the best emulators ever made. Excellent compatibility, upscaling, netplay. Vulkan backend essential on Android.
known_limitations: Mali GPU Vulkan drivers limit compatibility on some Android handhelds
A few games with unusual hardware features may have minor glitches
Needs Vulkan 1.1+ for best results on Android

systems.name: Nintendo Wii
systems.emulation_notes: Shares Dolphin with GameCube. Motion controls mapped to touch/gyro. Most games work perfectly.
known_limitations: Motion control games need touch/gyro mapping — not ideal on all handhelds
Wii Pointer games need IR emulation via touchscreen or gyro
Slightly more demanding than GameCube due to higher clocks

systems.name: PlayStation 2
systems.cpu: Emotion Engine @ 294.912 MHz + I/O Processor (MIPS R3000A)
systems.emulation_notes: AetherSX2 (paused development, NetherSX2 patch continues) and ARMSX2 (active) are the primary Android options. Vulkan driver quality is the #1 bottleneck. Qualcomm Adreno GPUs have significantly better compatibility than Mali.
known_limitations: Vulkan driver quality directly determines compatibility per-game
Mali GPU devices have much lower compatibility than Adreno
CPU-intensive games (God of War, Shadow of the Colossus) need strong SoCs
AetherSX2 development paused — NetherSX2 patches continue but no major updates
Per-game settings often required for best results

systems.name: Wii U
systems.emulation_notes: Cemu Android port is relatively new. Desktop version is more mature. Dual-screen (TV + GamePad) complicates handheld emulation.
known_limitations: Android port is still maturing — expect bugs
Dual-screen paradigm doesn't map well to single-screen handhelds
Very demanding on both CPU and GPU
Vulkan required for acceptable Android performance

systems.name: Nintendo Switch
systems.cpu: NVIDIA Tegra X1 (4x Cortex-A57 + 4x Cortex-A53) @ 1.02 GHz
systems.emulation_notes: Eden (Yuzu fork) on Android — Qualcomm Adreno + Turnip Vulkan drivers practically required. Mali GPUs are mostly non-functional. x86 platforms (AMD/Intel) have better compatibility. Still an active platform with ongoing game releases.
known_limitations: Qualcomm Adreno with Turnip drivers required for Android
Mali GPU Vulkan drivers cause widespread incompatibility
Many AAA titles unplayable or severely degraded
Legal grey area — Yuzu project was shut down, Eden is a community fork
Firmware/key requirements create setup complexity
Active platform — newer games frequently break compatibility

systems.name: Game Boy
systems.emulation_notes: Trivially emulated. SameBoy is the most accurate but any core works perfectly.

systems.name: Game Boy Color
systems.emulation_notes: Same cores as Game Boy. Color palette handling is well-documented and accurate.

systems.name: Game Boy Advance
systems.emulation_notes: mGBA is the gold standard — fast, accurate, and actively maintained. Solar sensor and tilt games supported.
known_limitations: Link cable multiplayer emulation varies by core

systems.name: Sega Game Gear
systems.emulation_notes: Essentially a portable Master System with different resolution. Same cores handle it.

systems.name: PlayStation Portable
systems.emulation_notes: PPSSPP is one of the best-optimized emulators ever created. Runs full speed on even budget SoCs. Supports upscaling to 4K+, texture replacement, and post-processing.
known_limitations: A handful of games have rendering glitches
Some ad-hoc multiplayer games need specific networking plugins

systems.name: Nintendo DS
systems.emulation_notes: MelonDS is the current best option — accurate and supports Wi-Fi. Dual-screen layout needs screen arrangement options. DraStic was once the Android king but is now open source.
known_limitations: Dual-screen rendering increases CPU cost vs single-screen systems
Touchscreen input mapping varies by emulator and device
Microphone-dependent games need audio input routing

systems.name: Nintendo 3DS
systems.cpu: ARM11 MPCore dual-core @ 268 MHz (New 3DS: quad-core @ 804 MHz)
systems.emulation_notes: Azahar (Citra community fork) and Citra MMJ for Android. New 3DS-exclusive games are more demanding. Stereo 3D not emulated. Citra MMJ often performs better on ARM handhelds than official builds.
known_limitations: Original Citra project shut down — Azahar is the community continuation
New 3DS-exclusive titles need more CPU power
Dual-screen layout complicates single-screen handhelds
Some games have shader compilation stutters on first run
StreetPass/SpotPass features not emulated

systems.name: MS-DOS / IBM PC
systems.emulation_notes: DOSBox Pure via RetroArch provides excellent DOS compatibility. Auto-configuration of CPU speed, sound cards, and memory. ScummVM covers point-and-click adventures separately.
known_limitations: Protected-mode games may need specific DOS extender configurations
Sound card emulation (Sound Blaster, Roland MT-32) varies by game era
Some late-DOS games pushing 3D (Quake, Duke3D) need higher CPU emulation speed

systems.name: Point-and-Click Adventures
systems.emulation_notes: ScummVM is not an emulator — it reimplements game engines. Supports 300+ games across dozens of engines (SCUMM, SCI, AGI, Wintermute, etc.). Runs on anything.
known_limitations: Game data files must be legally owned
Some engines are less mature than others (check ScummVM compatibility list)

systems.name: Windows PC Games
systems.emulation_notes: Winlator uses Wine + Box86/Box64 translation to run Windows x86 games on ARM Android. Only practical on flagship SoCs (SD 8 Gen 2+, Dragonwing Q8). DirectX translated to Vulkan via DXVK.
known_limitations: Only flagship ARM SoCs have enough power
x86-to-ARM translation adds significant overhead
DirectX → Vulkan translation (DXVK) introduces compatibility gaps
Anti-cheat software (EAC, BattlEye) does not work
Modern AAA games are generally too demanding
Configuration is complex — per-game profiles often needed
